title: Reliquary Blueprint
description: Synchronized companion to the composed blueprint model (planning/design/blueprint-model.md), which remains normative. One authored JSON kind, .rlqb: an array of specs of two types, machine and media, with a lone spec object accepted as sugar for the array of one and a bare string as a media located by it. type defaults to media. Schema validity never implies document validity: the name charter's derivation and repair, identity dedup and case collision, the reference grammar and its closure, containment paths and cycles, sha256-required-once-remote, medium compatibility, and every backend capability check live in the specification and the parser only. Note what this schema deliberately does NOT do: the closed vocabularies below stay plain enums and are never widened to admit a reference pattern, which is exactly what makes editor completion work on them. It validates the parsed document; the JSONC dialect (comments, trailing commas) is invisible at this level. Documents carry no $schema field pre-1.0; editors bind this schema to *.rlqb by file association. The machine state (machine.json) is a separate document type with its own schema (machine-state.schema.json).

oneOf.description: The general form: an array of specs.

spec.description: One spec: a machine, a media, or a bare string desugaring to a media located by it.

mediaName.description: The media-name charter: a letter or digit, then letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-'. Whitespace, braces, '#', '/' (the containment separator) and control characters are out by grammar; parens and brackets by argv, every media name being a command-line argument.

machine.description: Machine topology only. A drive names a media, is empty, or carries one written in place; content and materialization live on the media. A machine must declare its type, since type defaults to media everywhere.

platform.description: The guest platform. Required, never inferred, and never supplied by a reference.

backend.description: The materializing backend. Never supplied by a reference.

memory.description: A size string, a whole-MiB integer, or a reference supplying one.

devices.description: Devices the machine must contain, as a portable declared fact: assignment finds a backend that provides every one, and a host where none can refuses naming the device. The vocabulary is curated and grows one name at a time, as demand for a device arrives.

items.description: A closed vocabulary: never widened to admit a reference pattern.

propertyNames.description: Slot keys are fixed and never take a reference: an object key is authored graph.

items.description: A closed vocabulary: never widened to admit a reference pattern.

drive.description: A media name, null for a declared-but-empty removable slot, a hardware-attribute object, or a media written in place.

controller.description: A closed vocabulary: never widened to admit a reference pattern.

media.description: A media spec. name is optional here: it may be derived from content, or absent entirely for the anonymous blank at a drive - both rules beyond this schema.

materialize.description: A closed vocabulary: never widened to admit a reference pattern.

not.description: A blank takes a size, not a location.

child.description: A children entry: a media declared in place, in path form only - its location is its parent plus that path. A bare string is the path.

path.description: Static: a containment path never takes a reference, because the catalog can never depend on a download.

sha256.description: A hex SHA-256, or a reference supplying one - a hash is not a closed vocabulary, so it stays interpolable.

location.description: One rung, or a flat mirror list of them tried in order. Strings are interpreted by scheme; objects are the canonical form and the option point.

oneOf.description: The local form: a host path, relative to the referencing file.
The containment form: a media name or an inline media spec, with an optional path. No path means the parent's own bytes.
The property form: supplied through the property chain.
